definitions.explanation: A count of six items using the counter {本|ほん}, which applies to long, thin objects such as pens, bottles, sticks, trees, films, calls, and roads.

examples.japanese: ビールを{六本|ろっぽん}{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought six bottles of beer.

examples.japanese: ペンが{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{六本|ろっぽん}{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Six pens are lined up on the desk.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}の{周|まわ}りには{大|おお}きな{松|まつ}の{木|き}が{六本|ろっぽん}{植|う}えられている。
examples.english: There are six large pine trees planted around the house.

notes:
{六|ろく} (six) + {本|ほん} (counter for long, thin items), with sokuon and the regular {本|ぽん} → {本|ぽん} change yielding ろっぽん.

SOUND CHANGES WITH {本|ほん}:
- {一本|いっぽん}, {二本|にほん}, {三本|さんぼん}, {四本|よんほん}, {五本|ごほん}, {六本|ろっぽん}, {七本|ななほん}, {八本|はっぽん}, {九本|きゅうほん}, {十本|じゅっぽん} / {十本|じっぽん}

The ぽん/ぼん/ほん alternation follows the same pattern as other counters using {本|ほん}.

TYPICAL USES:
- ビール{六本|ろっぽん}: six bottles of beer
- {鉛筆|えんぴつ}{六本|ろっぽん}: six pencils
- {映画|えいが}{六本|ろっぽん}: six films
- {電話|でんわ}{六本|ろっぽん}: six phone calls

NOTE: {六本木|ろっぽんぎ} (Roppongi, a district in Tokyo) literally means 'six trees' and uses this same counter.
